quote: First off, I've got your address here as 265 Shadow Glen Court in Gettysburg, Maryland. Is that correct?
stewart_read: The rep reads the address but the transcript shows no clear customer confirmation before the rep moves to 'Let me pull that up here' — a hard-DQ-relevant verify item (homeowner/address) is left unconfirmed on the record.
alternative_hypothesis: The customer may have confirmed off-mic or the diarization dropped a short 'yes' — but nothing in the transcript supports that, so it should be treated as unconfirmed rather than assumed.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to get an explicit verbal yes on address/homeowner status before moving on — this is a hard-DQ gate item (renters can't buy solar) and shouldn't be assumed complete.

quote: let me also check what are the subsidy, how much the thing that is. I'm just checking.
stewart_read: Customer raises a subsidy/incentive question that borders on closer-tier financial content. The rep does not address it directly in the transcript — he moves straight to 'Yeah. Okay. So you're just kinda seeing what solar would look like for you?' without answering or bridging to the specialist.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep could be strategically deferring this to the closer without saying so explicitly, but there's no escape-hatch language used ('the specialist will walk you through that') — so this reads as an unaddressed gap rather than a deliberate bridge.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to use the universal escape hatch explicitly when subsidy/tax-credit questions come up — even a one-line 'our specialist will break down exactly what you qualify for' closes the loop instead of silently skipping it.

stewart_read: The customer's answer trails off after 'Between... 50' and the rep supplies the rest of the range himself ('to 300? Okay.') without an explicit re-confirmation that this is accurate. This is ambiguous: it could be the rep finishing a sentence he half-heard, or the rep guessing a number the customer never stated cleanly.
alternative_hypothesis: If the customer had actually said '50 to 300' clearly and the diarization just clipped it, this would be a clean bill capture — but as transcribed, the rep is the one voicing the full range, which is a coaching-relevant distinction between confirmed data and rep-supplied data.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to repeat the number back as a question ('so about $300 a month?') and wait for explicit confirmation rather than filling in an incomplete answer himself — this protects the accuracy of the anchor the whole design depends on.

quote: That is quite high, so we'll definitely help get that cut down for you.
stewart_read: The rep acknowledges the bill is high and moves on — capture-and-drop rather than capture-and-flip. He never turns the number into the customer's own reason to act later in the call.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive is the better read here: nothing later in the call (no appointment-set moment, no closing tieback) shows the bill being used as leverage, so there's no strategic deferral to point to.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to tie the bill number back into the ask later — e.g., referencing it when pushing for the bill document or when setting expectations for the closer call.

quote: yeah, your home here, it looks like a really good home for solar. You have a perfect southern exposure, which is super ideal for solar.
stewart_read: Rep proactively surfaces a positive qualifier (southern exposure) which is good technical framing, though this edges toward feature-selling rather than curiosity-creation.
coaching_implication: This is fine as a light credibility note, but the rep should avoid expanding on technical solar advantages further — keep it brief and pivot back to qualification, which he mostly did here.

quote: And then you could just I can't do it right now. I'll maybe it'll give me some text.
stewart_read: Customer signals friction pulling up the bill online right now. The rep explains why the data is needed but doesn't offer the read-aloud alternative (schema's elderly_low_tech_protocol logic applies broadly to any live-pull friction) before conceding to a delayed send.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged a live read-aloud wasn't feasible given the customer's own deferral language ('maybe I'll send you later'), making the text-and-wait path reasonable — this is a defensible strategic call, not a clear miss.
coaching_implication: When a customer can't pull up the bill live, try one direct ask for a verbal kWh number before falling back to a delayed text — it's a fast, low-cost attempt that sometimes rescues same-call capture.

quote: Maybe go to another day for them ultimately.
stewart_read: No specific day or time is agreed anywhere in the call — the closing exchange is entirely passive ('I'll look forward to that, around the end of the day') with no locked next step owned by the rep.
coaching_implication: This call needs a hard next-step: 'I'll call you back tomorrow at 5pm if I haven't heard from you' or a specific appointment slot pending the bill — not an open-ended 'we'll keep in touch.'
